overall: FAIL: eight of the nine logically distinct assertion groups are fair, but the assistant-array assertion on a direct `anchorClaudeCache` call is not. The required final upstream shape is prompt-stated, yet the hidden assertion additionally dictates that the cache-anchor helper, rather than the repository’s separate passthrough normalization stage, perform the wrapping. No suite-wide timing, randomness, ordering, environment, or hidden-fixture concerns were found. Coverage gaps below are advisory and do not affect this fairness verdict.

taskSummary: The task asks for two Claude request-translation fixes. First, final upstream requests must contain at most four `cache_control` markers; existing router breakpoints should still be added when the client has remaining marker budget. Second, a message whose `content` is one block object must not be filtered out: the upstream form must retain the turn, normalize the object to a one-element array, and remove a client-provided marker from that block. Existing array-content translation must remain unchanged. The relevant integration paths are `prepareClaudeRequest` for translated Claude requests and `normalizeClaudePassthrough` followed by `anchorClaudeCache` for native-Claude passthrough requests.

tests.evidence: The prompt explicitly requires that “a translated request never carries more than four cache_control markers.” The tested helper is the final passthrough anchoring operation: `open-sse/handlers/chatCore.js:300-302` calls `anchorClaudeCache` after other reshaping, and `open-sse/translator/formats/claude.js:267-272` describes it as the re-anchoring policy that runs last.
tests.name: never emits more than four markers — `countMarkers(out) <= 4`
tests.qualityCheck: Fair, but the setup does not actually contain four client markers: `tool` accepts only `name`, so `tool("t2", { cache_control: CC })` silently ignores the second argument. The input has three client markers, although the old implementation still reaches five after adding router markers. Thus it catches this regression but does not directly exercise the prompt’s stated already-four-marker scenario.
tests.verifies: After calling `anchorClaudeCache`, the total markers counted across system blocks, tools, array message blocks, and bare-object message content is at most 4.

tests.evidence: The prompt requires the final upstream request to use a one-element array, but does not assign that normalization to `anchorClaudeCache`. Searches for `one-element`, `single object`, `content: text(`, `Array.isArray(msg.content)`, `anchorClaudeCache`, and `normalizeClaudePassthrough` across source, tests, docs, and docstrings found no pre-existing contract that `anchorClaudeCache` performs shape normalization. On the contrary, `open-sse/translator/formats/claude.js:267-271` says anchoring runs after steps that reshape messages, while `open-sse/handlers/chatCore.js:188-190` calls the explicitly named `normalizeClaudePassthrough` before the final anchor at `open-sse/handlers/chatCore.js:300-302`. A grounded alternative is to normalize single objects in `normalizeClaudePassthrough`; that produces the prompt-required dispatched body but fails this direct-helper assertion.
tests.name: wraps a single-object assistant turn — assistant exists and `Array.isArray(assistant.content) === true`
tests.qualityCheck: The end behavior is required, but the assertion pins an unstated implementation boundary. It couples content normalization to the cache-anchor helper even though the visible pipeline has a separate normalization stage.
tests.verifies: A role-`assistant` message remains findable after direct invocation of `anchorClaudeCache`, and that helper itself has changed its bare content object into an array.

tests.evidence: The exact count follows the visible anchoring policy in `open-sse/translator/formats/claude.js:267-270`: last tool plus last system plus last assistant, with this setup containing neither tools nor system. `open-sse/translator/formats/claude.js:296-313` produces one message anchor by preferring the last assistant and using a fallback only if none was anchored. The prompt additionally says the router must still add its breakpoints when budget remains.
tests.name: wraps and anchors assistant turn — `countMarkers(out) === 1`
tests.qualityCheck: Fair but shallow: counting one marker does not establish that it is on the assistant turn named by the test. A solution placing the marker on the final user block could pass.
tests.verifies: For a body with no system or tools and one bare assistant block between array user turns, direct `anchorClaudeCache` output contains exactly one marker in total; the assertion does not constrain which block carries it.

tests.evidence: The prompt explicitly says “such a turn is kept.” In this setup `u1` uniquely identifies that turn.

tests.verifies: After `prepareClaudeRequest`, exactly one output message has serialized content containing the controlled text `u1`; therefore the marked single-object user turn was not dropped or duplicated.
